thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Edge POP 'ord1' (us-central-ORD) reporting elevated packet loss and 5xx spike across CDN egress. Detected by edge-health at 1968700123. Severity: p2 -> paging oncall-network. Metrics: 5xx rate +12%, packet loss ~6-9% on egress paths to multiple ISPs.

oncall-network: Ack. I'm paged, joining. Anyone already on a bridge?

sre-alex: joining now. seeing 502/504 surge from ord1 -> origin, plus TCP retransmits on connections to ISP peers. traceroutes show high loss beyond our edge.

eng-lee: looking at our egress stack. No recent deploys to ord1 in last 24h per deploy-bot.

pm-zoe: I'm with support — are customers impacted? any high-visibility tenants?

support-dan: some app teams report rate-limited errors. Top affected: chat-search service (3 customers), ingestion pipeline (one enterprise). Error dashboards: https://dash.redwood/ord1/overview (internal)

cloud-noc: Hey, we see BGP flaps on our peering with ISP 'MidNet' for prefixes announced from ord1 egress (203.0.113.0/24). Flaps started ~1968700000. We're opening ticket with ISP now.

oncall-network: thanks. can we (a) shift traffic off ord1 to nearby POPs and (b) apply temporary origin fallback?

sre-alex: plan suggestion: 1) reduce ord1 CDN weight to 10% via cdn control to drain connections 2) update egress BGP prepends rollback? 3) enable origin fallback to us-central-s3 for static assets.

eng-lee: I can run the weight change. Command: ```
# emergency control plane change
cdnctl pop update --pop ord1 --weight 10 --dry-run=false
```
I'll also enable per-route fallback for static origins: ```
cdnctl route update --route /static --origin us-central-s3 --failover=true
```

oncall-network: go ahead when ready. put a small delay between steps so we can watch metrics.

eng-lee: executing weight change now.

deploy-bot: Deployment log: cdnctl pop update started by eng-lee at 1968700480.

eng-lee: weight update applied. ord1 -> weight 10%. monitoring.

sre-alex: metrics: 5xx down 70% in 3m, packet loss on egress to MidNet still present from ORD vantage but client impact reduced. Good.

cloud-noc: MidNet reports intermittent uplink saturation on their Chicago aggregate; they're throttling some prefixes. They've escalated to their network ops.

pm-zoe: customer impact summary for now: transient errors for small set of tenants, majority of traffic unaffected after shift. I'll draft an external note: "We experienced reduced availability for assets delivered from ORD POP between 13:00-14:00 UTC; mitigated by rerouting and fallback. Engineers continue to monitor."

support-dan: Received ACKs from affected customers; they're seeing improved behavior after ~5-7 minutes.

oncall-network: we should open an incident ticket and assign owner for postmortem. I'll create INC-2026-ORD-089.

oncall-network: INC-2026-ORD-089 created and assigned to sre-alex. Bridge: https://call.redwood/INC-2026-ORD-089 (internal)

sre-alex: taking incident lead. I'm switching pages to daytime oncall eng-lee for handoff. @eng-lee can you take operations while cloud-noc continues to push ISP contact?

eng-lee: I'm taking ops. continuing monitoring. I'll keep ord1 at 10% and prepare to scale down further if MidNet reports worsen. Also prepping BGP community tweak if agreed with cloud-noc.

cloud-noc: note — MidNet requests that we temporarily prepend our ASN on ORD-announcements for the affected prefixes to influence inbound path selection; they'll coordinate on their side if we do that. Recommend caution: may affect latency for some peers.

oncall-network: agree to avoid aggressive prepends for now unless worst-case. We'll keep draining traffic.

eng-lee: enabling per-route origin fallback and keepalive tuning on ord1 to reduce connection churn. Command applied.

deploy-bot: cdnctl route update complete at 1968700842.

sre-alex: monitoring shows steady state: 5xx back near baseline, packet loss still seen from our edge -> MidNet but with lower customer impact. We'll hold on full failover while ISP works their side.

pm-zoe: drafting customer comms now. ETA 10m.

support-dan: adding list of impacted customers to the incident ticket.

oncall-network: small handoff: my shift ends in 25m. @sre-alex please take over as primary contact. I'll leave notes in the ticket.

sre-alex: acknowledged. thanks for the handoff.

cloud-noc: MidNet confirms they cleared a congestion event at 1968703000 and are seeing stabilized peering. They recommend keeping ord1 drained for another 15-30m to avoid flap recurrence.

eng-lee: increasing ord1 weight to 30% to slowly reintroduce traffic. Command: ```
cdnctl pop update --pop ord1 --weight 30
```

deploy-bot: cdnctl pop update completed at 1968703220 (by eng-lee).

sre-alex: metrics look good after reintroducing: 5xx stable, latency within normal. We'll keep monitoring for 60m.

pm-zoe: customer note sent. key points: incident window ~1968700000-1968703200 UTC, root cause: upstream ISP congestion affecting ORD egress, mitigation: temporary traffic shifts and origin fallback, current status: service stable, follow-ups: postmortem scheduled.

oncall-network: closing the high-urgency paging loop. Bridge remains open for 1h for monitoring.

sre-alex: closing primary incident channel for active mitigation; moving to postmortem doc INC-2026-ORD-089/postmortem. Please add any logs, config diffs, and timeline.

eng-lee: leaving one actionable item: consider adding automatic POP-drain policy when egress loss >5% sustained for >3m to speed mitigation. Filing ticket: INFRA-3421.

pm-zoe: scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

cloud-noc: ISP (MidNet) confirmed they applied fixes; they'll follow up with their root cause and timeline to attach to our ticket.

support-dan: customers updated and happy with contingency.

sre-alex: thanks everyone. Incident graded p2, mitigated by traffic shift and origin fallback, final note: watch for repeat flaps with this ISP; consider peering remediation.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-ORD-089 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Updated at 1968703720.
